title: Foundations of Recursive Interval Algebras
content: Recursive interval algebras are built from \(R = \mathbb{Z}[\Omega^{-1}]\), where \(\Omega > 1\) is an integer, by repeated formation of ordered pairs.  The component operations \(\operatorname{pos}\) and \(\operatorname{len}\) define arithmetic between arbitrary finite depths by descent to scalars.  The finite levels realize commutative algebras with square-zero generators, and their path coordinates connect algebraic structure with a recursively weighted norm.  A sharp one-level multiplication estimate yields exact constants for prescribed, possibly unequal, depths, with all equality cases and their attainability over the original coefficient ring.  Both tensor orientations have fixed-block norm factorization and an exact criterion for mixed-depth inner-product factorization.  Integral exponential and logarithmic operations determine normalized consecutive-block decompositions of units.  Recursive derivative evaluation characterizes coefficient-ring preservation and gives sharp bounds on homogeneous inputs.  Across unrestricted finite depths, local boundedness on a fixed-scalar fiber holds exactly when all derivative data of order at least two vanish.  Degree scaling makes products contractive precisely on a Euclidean parameter ball, and outside that ball no finite depth-independent bound exists.  Tensor concatenation further gives sharp commutator and Jordan associator estimates, including block-length-dependent constants and arithmetic conditions for attaining their endpoints.
